unresolved_choices: The official Canadian 9RX 640 page, within the declared North American market, publishes 8.309 m overall length with front weights, excluding three-point hitch and coupler. That boundary applies to the selected code 4000 less-hitch base; the separately selected Category 5 drawbar remains modeled. Configuration-specific overall width and height remain unresolved.
The visible 2.980 m track envelope is evidence-derived from 2.218 m center spacing plus one 0.762 m belt width, not a manufacturer-published overall-width claim.
Track pad, drive-lug, sprocket, idler, midroller, frame, tensioning, oscillation and axle geometry are not published.

Selected North American articulation and oscillation limits are unresolved. The 36-degree articulation, 15-degree chassis oscillation and plus/minus 10-degree undercarriage values are retained only as cross-market AU/NZ references for conservative reconstructed comparator checks.
Articulation gudgeon, oscillation pivot, cylinders, anchors, hard stops and cab-to-frame transforms are not published for the selected configuration.
Exact body panels, cab/glazing, cooling, aftertreatment, lighting, hoses, wiring, ballast and service hardware remain unresolved.
Manufacturer colors, graphics, badges and decals are outside the public structural study.
boundary: MY2025 North American 9RX 640 code 9540RW candidate with JD14, e18, base 30-inch AG3500 tracks at 87-inch spacing, less PTO and less rear hitch. North American sources constrain identity, code selections, the Canadian model-page length excluding hitch, track belt and spacing, and the Category 5 drawbar. Articulated/oscillating topology and conservative visual ranges are reconstructed; AU/NZ motion figures are cross-market references only and do not establish selected North American limits. Longitudinal track-pod placement, overall width/height, belt mechanics and hidden articulation geometry remain derived, reconstructed or unresolved. Neutral unbranded visualization only; not manufacturer CAD, a traction model, an engineering solver, safety guidance or proof of one delivered serial-number machine.
